# Computation

The computation is the `compare()` export of
[`mortgage.js`](/references/computations/mortgage.js). It reads
[`rates.json`](/references/data/rates.json) — the overnight-rate path,
the prime spread, and the best rates on offer at each pinned signing
month — and replays one contract of each kind month by month.

Canadian convention throughout: rates are annual, compounded
semi-annually. Each month is charged the rate in force on its first day.
Fixed-payment variables let unpaid interest capitalise past the trigger
rate; real lenders often intervene, so that branch is a ceiling on the
damage, not the typical outcome. The full list of assumptions and what
they cost is in [the article](/finance/fixed-or-variable.md#how-to-read-the-simulations-below).

## Running it

Follow [the executor](/references/executors/run-compare.md). It prints a
receipt carrying the SHA-256 of the computation and of the data it ran
against, the bound parameters, and the result.

## Checking a run

Pass that receipt to [the attester](/references/attesters/mortgage-attester.mjs).
It re-hashes the bundled computation and data, re-runs the computation
with the receipt's own parameters, and reports a verdict. A rewritten
computation, a swapped data file, or a result that does not match the
re-run all fail.

## Consumers

* [The article](/finance/fixed-or-variable.md) — every table is generated by this computation, never retyped.
* The in-page calculator on the human site — same module, loaded in the browser.
* [The video](/finance/fixed-or-variable-video.md) — every on-screen figure.
